Picture the makerspace assistant checking "is the laser cutter free Friday?" The model is like a receptionist at the front desk. A student asks her this, but she has no way to see the actual booking calendar herself — it's locked in a back office. So instead of guessing, she fills out a request slip: *"Tool: check_calendar. Equipment: laser cutter. Date: Friday."* She hands that slip through a window to the clerk in back.

That filled-out slip is a **tool call**: a request from the model to run one specific action, naming exactly which one (the tool) and the details it needs to run (the arguments). The important part — and this is the bit worth nailing down — the receptionist never touches the calendar herself. She can't; she only has a pen and a slip. The **clerk** (your program, the thing running the assistant) is the one who actually opens the calendar, looks it up, and does the real work. The model can only ever ask; something else outside the model carries the action out.

The clerk checks, writes "free 2–4pm" on a result slip, and passes it back through the window. The receptionist reads it — to her, it's now just more text in front of her, same as anything else — and turns it into an answer: "Yes, 2 to 4pm is open." If she'd needed another fact first, like whether the student is trained on the laser cutter, she'd have filled out a second slip before answering. That back-and-forth is the loop you already traced for me last time; a tool call is what each "ask for an action" step actually is under the hood.

Quick check: in your assistant, who actually holds the key to the real booking calendar — the model, or the program running it?
